info.name: Vanguard FTSE Social Index Fund Admiral Shares
info.description: The Vanguard FTSE Social Index Fund Admiral Shares aims to mirror the investment performance of the FTSE US Choice Index. This index is constructed from large and mid-capitalization stocks, weighted by their market value, and is subject to stringent environmental, social, and corporate governance (ESG) screening. The fund employs a passively managed, full-replication strategy, meaning it seeks to hold all the same securities as its benchmark index in similar proportions. A core principle of this index is the exclusion of companies involved in activities deemed socially irresponsible or controversial. Specifically, the index omits firms with significant engagement in: "Vice" industries: adult entertainment, alcoholic beverages, tobacco products, cannabis cultivation or distribution, and gambling operations. Controversial weaponry: the production of chemical and biological weapons, cluster munitions, anti-personnel landmines, nuclear weapons or components, conventional military weapons, or civilian firearms (including assault weapons and small arms). Fossil fuels and nuclear energy: companies involved in nuclear power generation, or those with substantial proven reserves or operations in coal, oil, and gas exploration, extraction, processing, or distribution, as well as electricity generation from oil, gas, or thermal coal. Beyond these sector-specific exclusions, the index disqualifies companies that fail to adhere to certain fundamental labor rights, human rights, environmental protection standards, or anti-corruption practices. Additionally, firms that do not satisfy specific diversity benchmarks—such as having at least one woman on the board, implementing diversity policies, and establishing diversity management systems—are also excluded. The index provider, FTSE, meticulously evaluates a company's level of involvement, revenue thresholds, and the severity of any controversies to apply these stringent criteria and determine eligibility across all exclusion categories, utilizing detailed internal methodologies. Furthermore, with respect to 75% of its total assets, the fund generally cannot acquire more than 10% of the outstanding voting securities of any single issuer, nor can an investment in any single issuer exceed 5% of the fund's total assets. This rule is waived if necessary to accurately replicate the target index's composition and does not apply to obligations issued by the U.S. government or its agencies.

info.name: Vanguard FTSE Social Index Fund Institutional Shares
info.description: This fund aims to replicate the performance of the FTSE US Choice Index. This benchmark is a market-capitalization-weighted index, encompassing both large and mid-sized U.S. companies. A core principle of the fund is its rigorous screening based on environmental, social, and corporate governance (ESG) criteria. Specifically, it divests from businesses operating in sectors such as adult entertainment, alcohol, tobacco, cannabis, and gambling. It also omits companies associated with the development or manufacturing of various armaments, including chemical and biological weapons, cluster munitions, anti-personnel landmines, nuclear weapons, conventional military weapons, and civilian firearms. Additionally, the index excludes firms involved in nuclear power, as well as the production or extraction of coal, oil, or gas. Beyond these industry-specific exclusions, it also filters out companies failing to uphold specific standards related to labor practices, human rights, environmental protection, and anti-corruption. Businesses that do not satisfy defined diversity benchmarks are also excluded. The fund utilizes a passive management strategy, aiming for full replication of its benchmark index. It's important to note that the index administrator, FTSE, employs specific methodologies to implement these exclusions. This involves assessing a company's level of involvement in a particular activity or the threshold amount of revenue it derives from such activities, which can vary across different sectors. For instance, companies are barred if they engage in production, distribution, or significant support roles within the excluded industries (e.g., manufacturing alcoholic beverages, owning gambling establishments, producing weapons components, or extracting fossil fuels, including detailed criteria for upstream, midstream, and downstream petroleum activities). Similarly, the non-compliance exclusions (labor, human rights, environmental, anti-corruption) are based on FTSE's internal assessment. For diversity, companies are excluded if they fail to meet at least two of these three criteria: having at least one woman on the board, established diversity policies, and functional diversity management systems. FTSE's internal analysis considers factors like revenue generation from an industry, the extent of company involvement, and the severity of any controversies. For at least 75% of its total assets, the fund operates under specific investment constraints: it cannot acquire more than 10% of the voting shares of any single company, nor can more than 5% of its total assets be allocated to the securities of a single issuer. These restrictions are waived only when necessary to accurately track the composition of the target index or when investing in U.S. government or agency obligations.

info.name: Vanguard Tax-Managed Capital Appreciation Fund Admiral Shares
info.description: This offering from Vanguard's suite of tax-optimized funds provides investors with exposure to U.S. equities, specifically targeting mid- and large-capitalization companies. It employs an index-replication strategy, striving to mirror its benchmark while actively seeking to suppress taxable capital gains and dividend payouts by selectively acquiring lower-dividend-paying stocks within the index. A notable risk for investors is the fund's allocation to mid-cap stocks, a segment typically prone to higher volatility than large-capitalization securities. This fund is generally suited for sophisticated investors in elevated tax brackets who possess a long-term investment horizon of at least five years and a robust appetite for risk, serving as a potential enhancement to a diversified investment strategy. However, it is crucial to recognize that the fund might not always achieve its intended tax-efficiency objective. Furthermore, specific investment limitations apply to three-quarters of its assets: it cannot acquire over 10% of any single issuer's outstanding voting shares, nor can more than 5% of the fund's total assets be allocated to one issuer's securities. info.name: Vanguard Total Stock Market Index Fund Institutional Shares
info.description: Launched in 1992, the Vanguard Total Stock Market Index Fund aims to provide investors with comprehensive exposure to the entire American stock market. Its primary advantages include notably low expenses, extensive portfolio diversification, and the possibility of favorable tax treatment. For individuals seeking an economical means to achieve broad U.S. equity exposure – and who are prepared for the inherent fluctuations of the stock market – this fund serves as an excellent option. It can function as either a foundational component of an investment portfolio or as the sole allocation to domestic stocks. Regarding 75% of its total assets, the fund operates under specific constraints: it cannot acquire more than 10% of a single company's outstanding voting shares. Furthermore, it is generally prohibited from investing more than 5% of its total capital in any one issuer's securities, unless such an allocation is essential for accurately mirroring its benchmark index. These restrictions do not, however, extend to investments in U.S. government debt or securities issued by its associated entities.

It employs a disciplined investment process, focusing on companies with strong financial characteristics and attractive growth prospects. Nuveen Asset Management, headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, manages the fund.

profile.description: The Fund seeks capital appreciation by investing primarily (at least 80% of net assets, plus the amount of any borrowings for investment purposes) in common stocks of large-capitalization companies.

FSKAX.name: Fidelity Total Market Index Fund
FSKAX.summary: Fidelity Total Market Index Fund seeks to provide investment results that correspond to the total return of the entire U.S. stock market. The fund invests in a broadly diversified portfolio of stocks of U.S. companies. Fidelity Management & Research Company is headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts.

profile.description: The Fidelity Total Market Index Fund typically allocates a minimum of 80% of its assets to U.S. equities that comprise the Dow Jones U.S. Total Stock Market Index. This particular benchmark is designed to track the overall performance of a wide spectrum of American companies. To achieve returns similar to the index without holding every single security, the fund's management team utilizes a statistical sampling methodology. This involves evaluating specific characteristics such as market capitalization, industry representation, dividend payouts, price-to-earnings (P/E) multiples, price-to-book (P/B) ratios, and expected earnings growth to select a more focused portfolio.

GOODX.name: GoodHaven Fund
GOODX.summary: The GoodHaven Fund is a long-term oriented investment fund that seeks to generate attractive returns by investing in undervalued companies with strong management teams and sustainable competitive advantages. The fund managers employ a value investing approach, focusing on in-depth fundamental research to identify investment opportunities. The fund is managed by GoodHaven Capital Management, based in New York.

FBGRX.name: Fidelity Blue Chip Growth Fund
FBGRX.summary: Fidelity Blue Chip Growth Fund seeks capital appreciation by investing primarily in common stocks of blue chip companies. The fund focuses on companies with above-average growth potential. Fidelity Management & Research Company LLC manages the fund.

profile.description: This fund predominantly invests in equity shares. It typically commits a minimum of 80% of its assets to blue-chip companies, which Fidelity Management & Research Company LLC (FMR) defines as well-known, established, and well-capitalized enterprises, generally having large or medium market valuations. The portfolio includes securities from both domestic and international entities. Investment choices are guided by a thorough fundamental analysis, examining factors like an issuer's financial health, industry competitive position, and broader market and economic trends.

CAMLX.name: Congress Large Cap Growth Fund Retail Class
CAMLX.summary: Congress Large Cap Growth Fund Retail Class seeks long-term capital appreciation by investing primarily in a diversified portfolio of large-capitalization growth stocks. The fund focuses on companies with strong earnings growth, innovative products or services, and experienced management teams. Congress Asset Management, based in Boston, Massachusetts, manages the fund.

ESEIX.name: Eaton Vance Atlanta Capital Select Equity Fund Class I
ESEIX.summary: Eaton Vance Atlanta Capital Select Equity Fund Class I seeks long-term capital appreciation by investing primarily in a diversified portfolio of equity securities. The fund is managed by Eaton Vance, headquartered in Boston, MA, and sub-advised by Atlanta Capital Management. It utilizes a fundamental, bottom-up approach to select securities.

GINDX.name: Gotham Index Plus Fund Institutional Class
GINDX.summary: Gotham Index Plus Fund Institutional Class seeks to outperform its benchmark index by employing a long/short equity strategy. The fund combines index exposure with quantitative stock selection to generate alpha. Gotham Asset Management, headquartered in New York, manages the fund.

profile.description: The Gotham Index Plus Institutional fund employs an "enhanced index" or "index plus" strategy, distinguishing it from a traditional passive index fund. Its investment approach involves taking both long and short positions in equity and equity-related securities. A segment of the fund's assets is dedicated to mirroring the performance of the S&P 500® Index. Complementing this, the fund also gains exposure through an actively managed long/short portfolio. This additional portfolio primarily invests in the 500 to 700 largest U.S. companies by market capitalization, utilizing both long and short holdings.

MGRPX.name: Morgan Stanley Institutional Fund, Inc. Growth Portfolio Class IS
MGRPX.summary: Morgan Stanley Institutional Fund, Inc. Growth Portfolio Class IS invests primarily in equity securities of companies believed to have above-average growth potential, seeking long-term capital appreciation. The fund focuses on identifying companies with strong earnings growth and innovative business models. Morgan Stanley Investment Management, headquartered in New York, manages the portfolio.

HWAIX.name: Hotchkis & Wiley Value Opportunities Fund Class Institutional
HWAIX.summary: Hotchkis & Wiley Value Opportunities Fund Class Institutional seeks long-term capital appreciation by investing primarily in equity securities considered to be undervalued. The fund employs a value investing strategy, focusing on companies with low price-to-earnings, price-to-book, and price-to-cash flow ratios. Hotchkis and Wiley Capital Management, LLC manages the fund.

profile.companyName: Hotchkis & Wiley Opportunities Fund Class I
profile.description: The Hotchkis & Wiley Value Opportunities Fund Class Institutional seeks to achieve long-term capital appreciation. Its portfolio typically comprises a diverse range of equity securities, including common, preferred, and convertible shares from companies of varying market capitalizations. Additionally, it invests in both high-quality (investment-grade) and higher-risk, higher-yielding ("junk") fixed-income instruments. The fund's approach focuses on identifying businesses whose future potential is either underestimated or not fully grasped by the wider market. It implements a fundamental value investment methodology designed to capitalize on market inefficiencies arising from emotional or illogical investor behavior. Notably, the fund operates as a non-diversified portfolio.

quote.name: Hotchkis & Wiley Opportunities Fund Class I

MFELX.name: MFS Growth Fund Class R1
MFELX.summary: MFS Growth Fund Class R1 seeks capital appreciation by investing primarily in common stocks of companies with above-average growth potential, while considering factors such as industry trends and economic conditions, and may invest in foreign securities. The fund's investment strategy focuses on identifying companies with sustainable growth prospects and strong management teams. The fund is managed by MFS Investment Management, headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts.

JGASX.name: JPMorgan Growth Advantage Fund Class I
JGASX.summary: JPMorgan Growth Advantage Fund Class I seeks long-term capital appreciation by investing primarily in equity securities of companies with above-average growth potential. The fund focuses on companies with strong earnings growth, innovative products or services, and experienced management teams. JPMorgan Investment Management Inc. manages the fund.

AULDX.name: American Century Ultra Fund R6 Class
AULDX.summary: American Century Ultra Fund R6 Class seeks long-term capital growth by investing primarily in common stocks of established, large-cap companies that are believed to have above-average growth potential. The fund is managed by American Century Investments, headquartered in Kansas City, Missouri, focusing on fundamental research and a growth-oriented investment approach. American Century offers a broad range of investment strategies across various asset classes.

profile.description: The American Century Ultra Fund primarily invests in the equity securities of businesses that the advisor anticipates will experience significant long-term appreciation. Its investment strategy is centered on thorough, company-specific analysis, rather than relying on broader economic forecasts. The portfolio managers employ diverse analytical research tools and techniques to pinpoint larger capitalization companies that align with their specific investment standards. Typically, the fund targets companies that are not only expanding their earnings or revenues but are doing so at an increasing rate.

USSPX.name: USAA 500 Index Fund Member Shares
USSPX.summary: USAA 500 Index Fund Member Shares aims to track the performance of the S&P 500 Index. The fund offers investors broad exposure to large-cap U.S. equities. USAA Investments manages the fund, employing a passive indexing strategy.

profile.description: Under typical market conditions, the fund primarily dedicates a minimum of 80% of its assets to investing in the equities of companies included in its benchmark index. To replicate the index's performance, the appointed sub-advisor endeavors to strategically distribute the fund's capital across these holdings, striving for similar proportional weightings as the index, with an initial emphasis on the companies that represent the largest portions of the index's total value.

QALGX.name: Federated Hermes MDT Large Cap Growth Fund Class A Shares
QALGX.summary: Federated Hermes MDT Large Cap Growth Fund Class A Shares seeks long-term capital appreciation by investing primarily in equity securities of large-cap companies with above-average growth potential. The fund utilizes a quantitative investment approach to identify companies with strong earnings growth and attractive fundamentals. Federated Hermes, headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, manages the fund.

KDHIX.name: DWS CROCI Equity Dividend Fund - Class Inst
KDHIX.summary: The DWS CROCI Equity Dividend Fund - Class Inst seeks to provide current income and long-term growth of capital. It invests primarily in dividend-paying equity securities of companies that DWS Investment Management Americas, Inc. believes are undervalued based on its CROCI (Cash Return on Capital Invested) methodology. DWS Investment Management Americas, Inc. is headquartered in New York City.

EILVX.name: Eaton Vance Large-Cap Value Fund Class I
EILVX.summary: Eaton Vance Large-Cap Value Fund Class I seeks long-term capital appreciation by investing primarily in equity securities of large-capitalization companies believed to be undervalued. BFTUX.name: Baron Fifth Avenue Growth Fund Class R6

OGRIX.name: Invesco Comstock Select Fund Class R6
OGRIX.summary: The Invesco Comstock Select Fund Class R6 seeks capital appreciation and income by investing in a diversified portfolio of common stocks, bonds, and money market instruments; Invesco is headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia. The fund uses a flexible asset allocation strategy, adjusting the mix of stocks, bonds, and cash based on market conditions and economic outlook. It aims to provide a balance of growth and income for investors.

PLFMX.summary: Principal LargeCap S&P 500 Index Fund R-3 Class seeks to replicate the performance of the S&P 500 Index by investing primarily in the stocks that make up the index. The fund aims to provide investors with broad exposure to the U.S. large-cap equity market at a low cost. This index is designed to broadly represent the risk and return characteristics typical of large-capitalization U.S. equities.

GEGTX.name: Columbia Large Cap Growth Fund Institutional Class
GEGTX.summary: Columbia Large Cap Growth Fund Institutional Class seeks long-term capital appreciation by investing primarily in equity securities of large-cap U.S. companies with above-average growth potential. The fund focuses on companies with strong earnings growth, innovative products or services, and capable management teams. Columbia Threadneedle Investments manages the fund.

MIEAX.name: MM S&P 500 Index Fund Class R4
MIEAX.summary: MM S&P 500 Index Fund Class R4 seeks to replicate, before fees and expenses, the performance of the S&P 500 Index. MassMutual is based in Springfield, Massachusetts.

PAGRX.name: Permanent Portfolio Aggressive Growth Portfolio Class I
PAGRX.summary: The Permanent Portfolio Aggressive Growth Portfolio Class I seeks long-term capital appreciation through investments in a diversified portfolio of asset classes, employing a tactical asset allocation strategy. The fund aims for aggressive growth and is actively managed by the Permanent Portfolio Family of Funds. The firm is based in Austin, Texas.

profile.description: The fund invests in stocks and stock warrants of U.S. and foreign companies that are expected to have a higher profit potential than the stock market as a whole and whose shares are valued primarily for potential growth in revenues, earnings, dividends or asset values rather than for current income.

NCGFX.name: New Covenant Growth Fund
NCGFX.summary: New Covenant Growth Fund's investment objective is capital appreciation, mainly by investing in companies with strong growth potential and long-term viability. The fund's investments are guided by Christian values. The headquarters location is unknown.

profile.description: Ordinarily, the fund's investment strategy centers on building a diverse portfolio of U.S. equities. These holdings are typically constituents of an index engineered to provide broad exposure to the American stock market. However, the advisor employs a rigorous screening process to exclude certain types of companies. Specifically, the fund abstains from investing in enterprises involved in tobacco, alcohol, or gambling, as well as for-profit prison operations. This exclusionary policy also extends to particular weapons manufacturers, including those producing antipersonnel mines, handguns, and assault weapons. Furthermore, the fund may, at its discretion, divest from or avoid companies implicated in serious human rights violations.

MIEZX.name: MM S&P 500 Index Fund Class R5
MIEZX.summary: MM S&P 500 Index Fund Class R5 seeks to replicate, before fees and expenses, the performance of the S&P 500 Index. This strategy is enhanced by investments in short-maturity, high-quality fixed income securities selected for their ability to deliver superior returns. The portfolio manager's objective is to replicate an equity benchmark that comprises a diverse cross-section of prominent large-cap corporations operating within the most significant sectors of the U.S. economy.

LGLRX.name: Lord Abbett Growth Leaders Fund Class R3

LLC, headquartered in Jersey City, New Jersey, using a growth-oriented investment approach that focuses on companies with above-average growth potential.

BIOPX.summary: Baron Opportunity Fund Retail Class seeks long-term capital appreciation by investing in a portfolio of growth-oriented equity securities across various market capitalizations. The fund is managed by Baron Capital Group and focuses on companies with strong growth potential. The fund's strategy involves fundamental research and a long-term investment horizon.

profile.description: This fund predominantly directs its investments into common shares of American companies characterized by rapid growth, encompassing businesses of all market sizes. The primary criterion for selection is the potential for significant increases in stock value. While the fund manager has the flexibility to explore opportunities across diverse sectors and industries, the strategy particularly emphasizes enterprises expected to capitalize on groundbreaking technological innovations and developments.

TIRTX.name: TIAA-CREF Large-Cap Growth Fund Retail Class
TIRTX.summary: The TIAA-CREF Large-Cap Growth Fund Retail Class seeks long-term capital appreciation by investing primarily in a diversified portfolio of equity securities of large-cap companies with growth potential. The fund is managed by Teachers Insurance and Annuity Association of America-College Retirement Equities Fund, based in New York, NY.

profile.description: Under typical market conditions, this fund is committed to investing a minimum of 80% of its total assets in large-capitalization equity securities. Its primary focus is on the stock of substantial U.S. companies, identified by the fund's benchmark index, which its investment adviser believes offer compelling growth opportunities. The fund also actively seeks out businesses poised to benefit from specific corporate events such as mergers, reorganizations, corporate restructurings, or other unique situations. While primarily domestic, it retains the flexibility to allocate up to 20% of its portfolio to foreign investments. It is important to note that the fund operates as a non-diversified entity.

OALGX.name: Optimum Large Cap Growth Fund Class A
OALGX.summary: The Optimum Large Cap Growth Fund Class A seeks long-term capital appreciation by investing primarily in a diversified portfolio of equity securities of large-capitalization companies with above-average growth potential. The fund employs a growth-oriented investment style, focusing on companies with strong earnings growth, innovative products or services, and experienced management teams. ALPS Advisors, Inc manages the fund.

PSTNX.name: PIMCO StocksPLUS Fund I-3
PSTNX.summary: The PIMCO StocksPLUS Fund I-3 seeks to outperform the broad U.S. equity market by combining exposure to equities with active fixed income management. The fund uses derivatives to gain exposure to equity markets while investing in a portfolio of fixed-income securities across various sectors and maturities. PIMCO is located in Newport Beach, California.

APHTX.name: Artisan Focus Fund Institutional Shares
APHTX.summary: The Artisan Focus Fund Institutional Shares seeks long-term capital appreciation by investing in a concentrated portfolio of equity securities of companies located in the United States. The fund employs a fundamental, bottom-up investment approach, focusing on identifying companies with strong growth potential and sustainable competitive advantages, with a focus on a limited number of holdings. Artisan Partners, based in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, manages the fund.

ITHTX.name: The Hartford Capital Appreciation Fund Class R5

CONWX.summary: Concorde Wealth Management Fund is a fund managed by Concorde Wealth Management. It is designed for wealth management. Further information is not available.

MFRCX.summary: MFS Research Fund Class C seeks capital appreciation by investing primarily in common stocks of companies that MFS believes have favorable growth prospects. JRSSX.name: Janus Henderson U.S. Managed Volatility Fund Class S
JRSSX.summary: The Janus Henderson U.S. Managed Volatility Fund Class S seeks to provide long-term capital appreciation by investing primarily in U.S. equity securities while managing volatility through a dynamic asset allocation strategy. The fund's investment approach involves utilizing quantitative models to identify companies with attractive risk-adjusted return potential and adjusting the portfolio's exposure to equities based on market conditions. Janus Henderson Investors, located in Denver, Colorado, manages the fund.

Its primary objective is to deliver market-comparable returns while exhibiting reduced price swings over the entire market cycle, relative to the Russell 1000® Index. FLUAX.summary: The Fidelity Advisor Stock Selector Large Cap Value Fund Class A seeks capital appreciation by investing primarily in common stocks of large-cap companies that are considered to be undervalued. A key risk associated with this fund is its allocation to mid-cap stocks, which inherently tend to experience greater price volatility compared to larger, more established companies. Individuals in higher tax brackets who possess a long-term investment horizon, typically five years or more, and a substantial tolerance for risk, may find this fund to be a valuable complement to a well-diversified portfolio. These rules may be waived only when essential for aligning the fund's composition with its target index. Importantly, these restrictions do not extend to investments in obligations issued by the U.S. government or its various agencies and instrumentalities.

info.name: State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF
info.description: SPY is the best-recognized and oldest US listed ETF and typically tops rankings for largest AUM and greatest trading volume. The fund tracks the massively popular US index, the S&P 500. Few realize that S&P's index committee chooses 500 securities to represent the US large-cap space - not necessarily the 500 largest by market cap, which can lead to some omissions of single names. Still, the index offers outstanding exposure to the US large-cap space. It's important to note, SPY is a unit investment trust, an older but entirely viable structure. As a UIT, SPY must fully replicate its index (it probably would anyway) and forgo the small risk and reward of securities lending. It also can`t reinvest portfolio dividends between distributions, the resulting cash drag will slightly hurt performance in up markets and help in downtrends. SPY is a favored vanilla trading vehicle.

info.name: FT Vest Technology Dividend Target Income ETF
info.description: TDVI aims for an 8% annual distribution, before fees and expenses, over the annual dividend yield of the Nasdaq 100 Index. However, the delivery of the target income is not assured. Distributions stem from dividends from technology companies within the Nasdaq Technology Dividend Index and premiums from selling naked index call options. These options are European style, written at-the-money, and will have expirations of less than 30 days. Each week, TVDI attempts to bridge the difference between the dividend income of its equity portfolio and its target distribution by selling at-the-money, naked call options on the NDX and/or SPX or related ETFs. The income from stock dividends and option premiums is expected to be distributed monthly. Investors should be aware that selling naked index call options carries a high level of risk.

info.name: TappAlpha SPY Growth & Daily Income ETF
info.description: TSPY marks the issuer's inaugural exchange-traded fund, established with the goal of democratizing access to more sophisticated investment methodologies. The fund's core strategy involves acquiring shares of the SPDR S&P 500 Index Trust (SPY) and systematically selling call options daily to generate revenue. These derivative contracts can be written against the underlying SPY shares, the broader S&P 500 index (SPX), or the Cboe Mini-SPX Index (XSP). While primarily utilizing zero-days-to-expiration (0DTE) contracts, the options' maturities may extend up to one week. The portfolio manager aims to produce daily income, which is then distributed to investors on a monthly basis. The fund also maintains holdings in US Treasury securities to serve as collateral.
